newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Governor urges China to listen to HK views.
newsitem.headline: Governor urges China to listen to HK views.

text.p: Governor Chris Patten on Friday urged Beijing to listen to a variety of views on the future governance of the territory after China expelled two Hong Kong democracy activists.
"You can't simply freeze out majority opinion in Hong Kong," he told reporters. "You have to involve everybody in the decision making about the future of this territory, not just a chosen few."
Anxiety is growing about political freedom in Hong Kong after it reverts to China next July 1.
On Friday, China ordered Wong Chung-ki and Chui Pak-tai to leave the country after they tried to petition Beijing officials over the political future of the colony.
"This sort of thing wouldn't happen if senior Chinese officials were prepared to talk to representatives of majority opinion here in Hong Kong," Patten said.

"Last August, I think it was, (Chinese) Vice Premier Qian Qichen suggested that contacts with the democrats could be opened up and that a real debate with them could commence. I think the sooner we see that happen the better," he added.
In August, Qian said the Beijing-controlled Selection Committee, which will pick Hong Kong's future leader, should include people with different views on the pace of democratisation.
But China's recent crackdown on dissidents has increased jitters over future political freedom in the territory.

Chinese border officials on Thursday barred two other Hong Kong pro-democracy advocates, Andrew To and Chan Kwok-leung, from entering the country as they tried to cross the border together with Wong and Chui on the same mission.
All four activists had planned to petition an influential China-appointed committee that was meeting in Beijing on arrangements for the handover.
